# Provenance

Every constant in `data/constants.js`, grouped by source.
`npm run provenance` rewrites this file after it checks that each constant
has a ref and a known source tag (`wowf-export`, `wowf-designer`,
`classic-1.12`, `cataclysm`, `assumption`, `engineering`). A missing ref,
a ref made only of dashes (including an em dash), a placeholder ref,
or an unknown tag fails the command. The check case-folds the ref.
Dashes, underscores, colons, slashes, backslashes, and bars separate
words. Other punctuation and symbols are deleted, and whitespace is
collapsed. `TBD`, `TBD.`, `TBD:x`, `TBD/James`, `N/A`, `NA`, `?`, `??`,
`tbd later`, `tbd-later`, `tbd_later`, and `fill_in` fail, as does a ref
made only of punctuation or symbols, or one whose first word is `tbd`.
The phrases `fill in` and `No recorded owner decision` fail only as
whole words.

148 constants: 27 `wowf-export`, 5 `wowf-designer`, 49 `classic-1.12`, 1 `cataclysm`, 24 `assumption`, 42 `engineering`.

| `modifiers.stacking`                  | `assumption`    | `{ "attackPower": "flat", "critChance": "flat", "hitChance": "flat", "dodgeReduction": "flat", "parryReduction": "flat", "armorIgnore": "flat", "energyRegen": "flat", "energyCost": "flat", "resourceMax": "flat", "damage": "percent", "critDamage": "bonus", "haste": "haste", "duration": "percent" }` | modifier kind → stacking form | Developer, 26 Oct 2026, issue #96: a judgement call by the dev, not a decision by James. A guess at how WoW Forever combines the modifiers of one kind (js/modifiers.js)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | A guess at a game rule, the stacking model, so it is on the retune list. "flat" is (base + the sum of the add values) × the product of the mult values, so a chance or a cost adds in its own units. "percent" is base × (1 + the sum of the add values) × the product of the mult values, so "+x% damage" talents add together and a separate multiplier multiplies. "bonus" is the same as "percent", applied to the crit bonus (the multiplier minus one), so Lethality-style effects scale the bonus and not the whole hit. "haste" is the product (or sum) that haste.stacking selects, once per stack. "duration" is "percent" on the length of an aura, so the +15% a rank of Improved Slice and Dice multiplies the 9 to 21 seconds of the table (+45% at 3/3 is 9 × 1.45), and a separate multiplier would multiply (D8a, #119). These follow the Classic convention that talent percentages add and buffs multiply. If WoW Forever stacks a kind differently, change its form here and nowhere else. |

A guess at how WoW Forever combines the modifiers of one kind (js/modifiers.js)                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | A guess at a game rule, the stacking model, so it is on the retune list. "flat" is (base + the sum of the add values) × the product of the mult values, so a chance or a cost adds in its own units. "percent" is base × (1 + the sum of the add values) × the product of the mult values, so "+x% damage" talents add together and a separate multiplier multiplies. "bonus" is the same as "percent", applied to the crit bonus (the multiplier minus one), so Lethality-style effects scale the bonus and not the whole hit. "haste" is the product (or sum) that haste.stacking selects, once per stack. "duration" is "percent" on the length of an aura, so the +15% a rank of Improved Slice and Dice multiplies the 9 to 21 seconds of the table (+45% at 3/3 is 9 × 1.45), and a separate multiplier would multiply (D8a, #119). These follow the Classic convention that talent percentages add and buffs multiply. If WoW Forever stacks a kind differently, change its form here and nowhere else. | yes    |
